title: Using in utero electroporation to investigate the role of semaphorin-3A in radial migration of cortical neurons
protocol: Digest cortices from E16 rats using 0.125% trypsin.
Transfect dissociated neurons with different plasmids (5 μg for each) by electroporation using the Amaxa Nucleofector before plating into 35 mm dishes according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Perform western blotting as described previously.

Lysate the 2-day cultures of transfected cortical neurons in 0.2 ml lysis buffer (0.1% SDS, 1% NP-40, 50 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 2 mM EDTA, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM Sodium Orthovanadate, 40 μM PNPP, 1% Protease Inhibitor Cocktail Set I).
Dissect brains from P0 rats and section them coronally on a vibratome at 500 μm.
Dissect slices into different parts using fine forceps and lyse them separately in 0.1 ml lysis buffer in a tissue homogenizer.
Centrifuge lysates at 12,000 RPM for 25 minutes at 4°C. Collect the supernatant and denature it.
Separate samples by 10% SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and transfer them onto PVDF membrane.
Block membranes for 3 hours at room temperature in 5% BSA.

Incubate membranes overnight at 4°C with polyclonal antibody (neuropilin-1, R&D, 1:500; GFP, Molecular Probes, 1:3,000; Sema3A, Santa Cruz, 1:500) or monoclonal antibody (neuropilin-2, R&D, 1:500; Actin, Chemicon, 1:3,000; Tubulin, Sigma, 1:3,000; Cre-recombinase, Chemicon, 1:1,000).
Rinse membranes in TBS.
Incubate membranes with peroxidase-conjugated goat anti-mouse, goat anti-rabbit, or donkey anti-goat IgG (Bio-Rad, 1:10,000) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse membranes in TBS again.
Perform chemiluminescent detection with the ECL kit (Pierce).
Extract total RNAs from 2-d cultures of cortical neurons prepared from E16 rat cortices with Trizol reagent (Invitrogen).
Convert about 5 μg of total RNA to cDNA (RevertAid First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit, MBI Fermentas).
Use 1/20 of the reaction in a 50-μl PCR reaction (Takara).
Perform PCR with conditions: 94 °C for 30 seconds, 58 °C for 45 seconds, 72 °C for 30 seconds for 30 cycles.
Add a final extension at 72 °C for 10 minutes.
Visualize end reaction products on ethidium-bromide-stained 1.0% agarose gels.
Transfect plasmids by in utero electroporation, following previous methods.
Anesthetize multiparous Sprague Dawley (SD) rats or ICR mice at 16 d of gestation with 10% Chloral hydrate for rats (3.5 ml per kg body weight intraperitoneally).
Anesthetize multiparous Sprague Dawley (SD) rats or ICR mice at 16 d of gestation with 0.7% sodium pentobarbital for mice (10 ml per kg body weight intraperitoneally).
Prepare a mixture of EYFP and RNAi constructs at a ratio of 1:1 (6 μg/μl each) for electroporation of two vectors.
Expose uteruses.
Microinject 15-20 μg plasmids mixed with Fast Green (2 mg/ml) into the lateral ventricle of embryos by pressure through uterus.
Generate electric pulses using ElectroSquireportator T830.
Apply five repeats of 60 V for 50 ms to the cerebral wall, with an interval of 100 ms between each pulse.
In some experiments, inject BrdU (Sigma) at 100 μg/g body weight intraperitoneally twice every 30 minutes 24 hours after in utero electroporation.
Remove embryonic brains directly and fix them with 4% paraformaldehyde at appropriate ages for fluorescence immunostaining.
Remove postnatal brains and fix them in 4% paraformaldehyde after transcardial perfusion.
Cryopreserve fetal and postnatal brains in O.C.T. compound (Sakura) for fluorescence immunostaining.
Cut coronal brain cryostat sections of 35 μm on a freezing microtome.
Immediately process the sections for immunostaining using a three-step free-floating protocol at 4°C.
Block non-specific antigenic sites in 10% BSA plus 0.3% Triton X-100 overnight.
Incubate with primary antibodies overnight.
Incubate with secondary antibodies overnight.
Dehydrate fixed brains by dipping into a series of ethanol and xylene.
Embed tissues in paraffin and section them at 5 μm after dehydration.
Perform immunostaining by the HRP-DAB staining kit.
Re-hydrate sections.
Block nonspecific peroxidase activity with 3% H2O2 for 10 minutes.
Incubate sections in 0.1 M citric acid (pH 6.0) at 90°C for 20 minutes to retrieve antigen.
Rinse sections, incubate sections in blocking reagent for 45 minutes.
Incubate sections with primary antibody against Sema3A overnight at 4°C.
The following day, rinse sections and incubate sections in anti-goat biotinylated secondary antibody for 30 minutes.
Rinse sections and incubate sections in HRP-conjugated streptavidin for 30 minutes.
Rinse sections and react sections in DAB chromogen for 10 minutes.
Monitor the intensity of staining under a microscope to ensure proper intensity.
Dehydrate the slides in graded ethanols and xylene.
Cover-slipp slides under neutral balsam.
Hybridize the sections with 1 μg/ml Digoxin-labeled sense or antisense probes for 16 hours at 65°C in hybridization solution.
Wash the sections twice with 2 X SSC for 30 minutes at 65°C.
Treat sections with RNase A (1 μg/ml in 2 X SSC) at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Wash the sections twice with 0.2 X SSC for 30 minutes at 65°C to remove excess probe.
Incubate the sections with alkaline phosphatase-labeled anti-Digoxin antibody (Roche) at 4°C overnight.
Detect the hybridization signal with a detection solution (1 μl of NBT and 3.5 μl of BCIP in every ml of mixture of alkaline phosphatase buffer) in the dark at room temperature overnight.
Perform slice culture as described previously.
Dissect brains from E19, P0 or P3 rats in ice-cold Hanks' balanced salt solution (HBSS).
Embed dissected brains in 4% low-melting point agarose in HBSS.
Section embedded brains coronally on a vibratome at 300 μm.
Culture slices on a transparent porous membrane (0.45 μm pore size, Millipore) in a 6-well culture plate containing 1 ml of medium (DMEM, 10% horse serum, Gibico).
Fix cultured slices in 4% paraformaldehyde at 4 DIV.
Stain fixed slices with anti-GFP antibody by the method described above.
Transfect brain cells with EYFP or co-transfect with EYFP plus NP1-RNAi1 at E16.
Section the transfected brains coronally on a vibratome at 300 μm thickness at P1 in ice-cold HBSS.
Transfer slices to the surface of a transparent porous membrane (0.4 μm pore size, Millipore) in a 35 mm culture dish containing 1 ml medium (DMEM, 10% Fetal Bovine Serum, 2% B27, Gibico).
Incubate slices in the cell culture incubator for 1 hr to allow recovery from injury.
Seal the culture dish with parafilm and transfer it to a heat stage (37°C) at the confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 510).
Pre-incubate slices with exogenous factors for at least 4 hr in the incubator before observation on the microscope.
Illuminate the tissue with a 488-nm wavelength light.
Acquire Z-series stacks of confocal fluorescence images using a 20x lens every 15 min for 3 hr.
Reconstruct images using LSM Image Browser.
Trace images using Neurolucida software.
Analyze migration speed of EYFP-labeled neurons using Neuroexplorer.
Exclude stationary cells (migration distance < 10 μm in 3 hr) from analysis.
Score a minimum of 200 cells from at least 5 sections for each experiment.
Assess statistical significance (P < 0.01) using Student's t-test.
Use anti-neuropilin-1 antibody (polyclonal, R&D, 10 μg/ml).
Use Sema3A (R&D, 1 μg/ml).
Fuse images to produce a movie at 2 frames/s with QuickTime Player.
Perform the transwell chemotaxis assay as described previously.
Transfect brains with EYFP alone or co-transfected with EYFP plus NP1-RNAi1 construct at E16 by in utero electroporation.
Obtain transfected cells from IZ at E20 – P0.
Assay the migration of dissociated transfected cells using a Boyden transwell system with 5 μm pore size.
Coat both sides of the transwell overnight with Poly-D-Lysine at 30 μg/ml.
Add 750 μl of serum-free medium containing one fifth of one million dissociated transfected cells to the upper insert of a chamber.
Add 250 μl of serum-free medium, with or without reagents such as BDNF (Chemicon) and Semaphorin-3A (R&D), to the bottom chamber.
Change the medium 1 day after seeding to maintain the reagent gradient.
Two days after seeding, fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde.
Scrap cells attached to the upper side of the membranes thoroughly.
Immunostain cells attached to the bottom side of the membranes with anti-GFP antibody.
Analyze cells directly under a confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 510).
Count the numbers of transfected cells in the slices using Image-Pro Plus 5.1 software.
For frozen sections:
Count EYFP-labeled cortical neurons on brain sections across three different cortical zones (Layer II/III, Layer IV-VI, and VZ/SVZ/WM) at different developmental stages.
Analyze the distribution of transfected cortical neurons.
Count at least 10 sections per experiment (1 section per rat or mice).
For slice culture experiments:
Count EYFP-expressing cells along the radial axis of cultured slices over ten equally divided zones from the presumptive VZ to the pial surface.
Express the counts as the cumulative distribution of labeled cells along the radial axis of transfected slices.
Count a minimum of 7 sections per experiment (1-2 sections per rat).
Assess statistical significance using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
For morphological analysis:
Semi-automatically trace the Z-series stacks of confocal images using Neurolucida software.
Analyze the total length and branch number of each individual process in transfected neurons using Neuroexplorer program.
For neurons in P3 cortices:
Summate all segments of a process into a vector.
Measure the angle between this vector and the neighboring radial glial fiber using Neuroexplorer.
Draw a line \(OP\) from the center of soma \(O\) perpendicular to the pial surface \(P) and designate it as the radial axis.
Construct a circle with a radius of 50 μm centered at \(O).
Designate the point where this circle crosses the main dendrite as \(R).
Measure the angle between \(OP\) and \(OR (\angle POR)\) using LSM Image Browser.
Assess statistical significance (P < 0.01) using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
Carry out Sholl analysis for dendritic complexity by counting the number of crossings of dendrites that cross a series of concentric circles at 10 μm intervals from the soma.
Assess statistical significance (P < 0.01) using Student’s t-test.
Score a minimum of 130 cells from at least 10 sections (1 section per rat) for each experiment to analyze the morphology of transfected neurons.
